key_points: Zydus transforming from seasonal niche-brand portfolio into diversified wellness player with RiteBite Max Protein and Comfort Click acquisitions expected to comprise ~50% of revenue by FY27
Consolidated comparable sales CAGR projected to accelerate to 13.7% (FY26-29) from historical 6.5% (FY21-26) driven by high-growth acquisition platforms
EBITDA margins expanding 310bps to 16% by FY29 from 12.9% in FY26, supported by gross margin expansion and operating leverage despite variable cost base of Comfort Click
Comparable adjusted EPS CAGR of 23% over FY26-29 at attractive valuations (~37x/29x FY27ii/28ii) as structural growth acceleration remains unpriced
Legacy portfolio maintains genuine moat with category-leading market shares (Sugar Free 96.1%, Glucon-D 59.1%, Nycil 32.9%) supporting gross margins and pricing power
Seasonal exposure declining from ~34% in FY20 to ~15% in FY28 as acquired platforms scale; distribution runway with 0.7mn direct outlets versus 3mn for large-cap FMCG peers
ROIC expansion of 424bps and adjusted ROIC improvement of 1440bps projected over FY26-29 period driven by margin accretion and working capital optimization
catalysts: Comfort Click international expansion into North America with company balance sheet and manufacturing scale
RiteBite Max Protein penetration acceleration through Zydus distribution network to 0.7mn outlets
Gross margin expansion in acquired platforms through premiumization and category adjacency products
Sequential margin improvement as CC cost leverage materializes at higher revenue scales
Everyuth innovation-driven TAM expansion within scrubs and peel-off sub-segments
Working capital normalization and operational leverage realization from scaled acquired platforms
reports.summary: Zydus Wellness is initiating with a BUY rating and Rs650 price target (23% upside) as strategic acquisitions of RiteBite Max Protein and Comfort Click fundamentally reposition the company from a seasonally-dependent portfolio of mature legacy brands into a high-growth diversified wellness platform. The combined transaction delivers a 13.7% comparable sales CAGR versus historical 6.5%, while EBITDA margins expand 310bps to 16% by FY29, driving 23% adjusted EPS CAGR—one of the fastest growth rates in FMCG coverage—at valuations that remain attractive relative to the structural acceleration.
reports.connection_narrative: India's health and wellness consumption is structurally accelerating as rising middle-class disposable incomes, premiumization trends, and digital commerce penetration converge to drive growth in specialized nutrition, protein products, and vitamins-minerals-supplements categories—a secular tailwind that Zydus is positioning itself to capture across domestic and international markets. The protein nutrition and active-lifestyle segments represent high-growth categories commanding pricing power and gross margins significantly superior to traditional FMCG, and the shift from mature sugar-substitute and glucose-powder categories toward these expanding consumer health trends is the core driver behind the company's acquisition strategy. Zydus Wellness benefits structurally through three distinct mechanics: first, its legacy portfolio of market-leading brands in Sugar Free, Glucon-D, Nycil, Everyuth, and Nutralite provides the cash generation and distribution muscle to fund growth investments, maintaining category-dominant positions that support gross margins of 50-60% versus legacy FMCG peers at 40-50%; second, RiteBite Max Protein acquired in November 2024 taps the rapidly-growing protein nutrition and active-lifestyle segments where annual growth exceeds 18-20%, directly leveraging Zydus's 0.7 million outlet direct distribution network to scale from boutique into mass channels; third, Comfort Click acquired in August 2025 represents the company's entry into the vitamin-mineral-supplement platform with a proven D2C and digital-first business model across UK, EU, and US markets, providing gross margins near 80% while the company's balance sheet and manufacturing scale enable international expansion beyond current UK-EU focus. The deseasonalization benefit is material—seasonal revenue exposure falls from 34% in FY20 to just 15% by FY28 as high-growth RiteBite and Comfort Click platforms, which carry year-round demand profiles, scale to 50% of consolidated revenue by FY27, reducing dependency on weather-driven categories like Glucon-D and Nycil and creating a more predictable growth trajectory. EBITDA margin expansion of 310 basis points to 16% by FY29 is driven by legacy brand gross margin accretion through premiumization, operating leverage on fixed costs, and the mix benefit from acquiring high-margin platforms, with 85% of Comfort Click's cost base being variable ensuring margin scalability. The single most important catalyst to monitor is the velocity at which RiteBite Max Protein penetrates Zydus's distribution network—scaling from current ~1,500 outlets to 50,000+ outlets would unlock 3-4 years of high-teens growth and represent the earliest tangible proof point of the acquisition thesis; meanwhile, the key risk lies in execution complexity across three geographically and operationally distinct business units and the potential for margin pressure if acquisition integration costs exceed guidance or if competitive intensity rises in the high-growth protein and VMS segments.

Leadership position: ~40% share in domestic 2W clusters, ~75-80% in TFT clusters, ~65% in CV clusters
Q1FY27 revenue growth of 23.5% YoY driven by TFT penetration, plastics scaling and EV content
Sundaram Auto acquisition adds Rs 924 Cr revenue with 94-95% utilization; Rs 400 Cr capex planned to double capacity to Rs 2,000 Cr by FY28
Powertrain-agnostic portfolio with exposure to both ICE and EV platforms; secured programs with Ather, TVS, Honda, River, Simple Energy
FY26-FY29E CAGR: Revenue 19%, EBITDA 21%, PAT 24% with ROE/ROCE improvement to 22%/30%
catalysts: DICVS demerger regulatory and NCLT approvals expected
TFT cluster penetration doubling from 7-8% over next 2-3 years
Polymer capacity expansion from Rs 1,000 Cr to Rs 2,000 Cr by FY28
Export programs with Honda and discussions with European/US OEMs

reports.summary: Pricol Ltd is a leading automotive component manufacturer with dominant positions in instrument clusters and fluid management systems, positioned to benefit from vehicle electrification, premiumization and electronics content growth across two-wheelers, passenger vehicles and commercial vehicles. The proposed DICVS demerger into Pricol Autotech will create two focused platforms enabling sharper capital allocation and independent valuations, while strategic acquisitions and export expansion drive medium-term growth. With FY26-FY29E revenue/EBITDA/PAT CAGR of 19%/21%/24% and a BUY recommendation with 22% upside to target price of Rs 935, Pricol offers exposure to structural automotive trends through high-quality management and strong OEM relationships.
reports.connection_narrative: India's automotive industry is undergoing a structural transformation driven by three interconnected forces: the shift from basic analog instrument clusters to advanced digital and connected systems as vehicle electronics content rises; rapid two-wheeler premiumization with consumers trading up to higher-value platforms that command more sophisticated driver information systems; and accelerating electrification requiring new sensor, battery management and thermal control capabilities. These trends are creating a multi-year content expansion opportunity across every vehicle segment. Pricol sits at the epicenter of this transformation with commanding market positions—approximately 40 percent share in two-wheeler clusters domestically and an estimated 75 to 80 percent share in the higher-margin TFT cluster segment which is still only 7 to 8 percent penetrated and expected to double over the next two to three years. The company's vertical integration across injection molding following the Sundaram Auto acquisition, in-house electronics and software capabilities, and long-standing OEM relationships create formidable switching costs and enable early participation in new platform development cycles. Its powertrain-agnostic portfolio—from traditional fluid management systems to electric coolant pumps and battery management solutions—insulates the company from powertrain transition risk while allowing it to capture electrification-led content growth with programs already secured across Ather, TVS, Honda and new-age EV manufacturers. The proposed demerger of the DICVS division into separately listed Pricol Autotech will unlock value by allowing investors to apply distinct business-specific multiples to the high-growth electronics business versus the stable cash-generative ACFMS and precision plastics operations, while enabling each entity to pursue independent capital allocation and merger-acquisition strategies. The single most important catalyst to monitor is successful regulatory and NCLT approval of the demerger combined with TFT penetration acceleration, which could trigger re-rating toward higher growth multiples. The primary risk to watch is execution risk on the Rs 400 crore polymer capacity expansion program and ability to monetize this incremental capacity across new customers, which is critical to achieving the targeted 16 to 18 percent return on capital employed for the plastics business.

key_points: PW Online revenue compounded at ~74% CAGR over FY23-26 with 100m+ YouTube subscribers providing structurally lower customer acquisition costs
Online business expected to clock ~28% CAGR over FY26-30E; Pre-IND AS EBITDA margins improving from ~26% in FY26 to ~30% by FY28E
Offline network of 353 centers (expanded 233% CAGR from FY23-26) represents high-ARPU monetization layer with 80% of admissions from online base
PW operates in mass-market, low-density quadrant with ~5m paying students at ARPU of ~INR4,000 serving significantly underpenetrated education categories
Valuation on SoTP basis assigns 50x FY28E EV/EBITDA to online business and 15x to offline, with target price of INR200 implying 66% upside
catalysts: Online revenue acceleration from AI-led monetization and category expansion
Offline center maturation and utilization normalization
Penetration gains in foundation, state boards and government exams segments
Faculty standardization reducing dependence on star teachers in offline centers
reports.summary: Physicswallah, among India's largest education platforms with 100m+ YouTube subscribers, has built a capital-efficient business model combining free content acquisition with multi-layered monetization across online, hybrid and offline offerings. Online business dominates with 74% CAGR and structurally lower customer acquisition costs, while the rapidly expanded 353-center offline network provides higher-ARPU growth with most admissions sourced from the digital base. Valued at INR200 (66% upside) on sum-of-the-parts basis, the company benefits from India's significantly underpenetrated education market and potential for deep category expansion beyond flagship JEE/NEET exams.
reports.connection_narrative: India's education market remains structurally underpenetrated with only 20% online penetration in flagship JEE and NEET categories and below 1% penetration in foundation, state boards and government exams, creating a multi-decade runway for digital adoption driven by smartphone proliferation and rising aspirations across mass-market income segments. Physicswallah has emerged as the capital-efficient leader by pioneering a mass-market, low-density business model through its free-to-paid YouTube funnel that generates customer acquisition at structurally lower costs than performance-marketing-dependent peers, while maintaining zero incremental physical infrastructure per online user. The company's competitive moat derives from network effects embedded in its 350,000-student cohort scale in live classrooms, self-reinforcing content engagement averaging 104 minutes per learner, and a pricing pyramid spanning INR0 to INR50,000 that enables monetization across seven educational categories throughout a student's journey from Class 9 through professional exams. The offline expansion to 353 Vidyapeeth centers, while introducing higher capital intensity and local execution risks, strategically extends the digital flywheel by converting 80% of online learners into offline students and providing trust-building physical presence in Tier-2 and Tier-3 markets where digital credibility remains underdeveloped. Financial projections anticipate online revenue compounding at 28% through FY30E with EBITDA margins improving from 26% to 30% by FY28E as customer acquisition efficiencies and AI-led monetization mature, while the offline business is expected to reach 3% EBITDA margin by FY28E as newly opened centers mature and utilization normalizes. The most critical near-term catalyst to monitor is the offline business unit economics as center-level productivity and return on invested capital will determine whether this capital-migration strategy successfully enhances long-term shareholder value or dilutes the superior returns generated by the online platform. The primary execution risk lies in faculty attrition and training effectiveness, as the playbook evolution toward standardized smart-board infrastructure and centralized faculty training programs must successfully reduce dependence on star teachers to sustain student outcomes and brand perception, particularly as PW scales aggressively into semi-urban and rural markets.

key_points: SBIFUNDS is India's largest AMC with INR29.1t total QAAUM (INR12.6t MF, INR16.5t PMS, INR68b AIF)
MF QAAUM recorded 19% CAGR over FY21-26, equity CAGR at 33%, passive CAGR at 20%
Monthly SIP flows surged from INR25b (Mar'24) to INR40b (current), with 98% registered for >36 months
Industry-leading opex efficiency at 8bp of AUM in FY26, expected to decline to 7bp by FY28
Structural advantages: 23,265 SBI branches, 100m+ YONO users, 134,000+ distribution partners
Equity AUM share increased from 30% (FY21) to 46.4% (current), supporting yield expansion to 35bp
SIF business achieved INR35b QAAUM and 25.8% market share within quarters of launch
Revenue CAGR expected at 14% FY26-28, PAT CAGR at 16%, with 51-52% RoE
catalysts: SBI distribution network penetration - less than 2% of eligible customer base tapped
SIP flow trajectory and account additions
Yield expansion from equity mix shift and scheme launches
AIF and PMS business scaling
SIF segment growth with higher TERs
Operating leverage from tech investments and cost efficiency
reports.summary: SBI Funds Management is initiating coverage with a BUY rating and target price of INR720 (28% upside). As India's leading AMC managing INR29.1t in total QAAUM, SBIFUNDS benefits from India's structurally underpenetrated MF industry (21% of GDP vs. 126% in US), strong SIP momentum (INR40b monthly flows), and an unmatched distribution moat through SBI's branch network and YONO platform. The company expects 13% MF AUM CAGR and 14% revenue CAGR through FY28, supported by industry-leading 8bp opex efficiency, equity mix shift to 46%+ of portfolio, and emerging high-yield alternatives, translating to 16% PAT CAGR and 51-52% RoE.
reports.connection_narrative: India's mutual fund industry represents one of the most compelling structural growth opportunities in global capital markets, with AUM-to-GDP penetration at just 21 percent against a developed market average of 75-126 percent, creating a multi-decade tailwind as household savings systematically shift from bank deposits toward financial assets. Simultaneously, the SIP revolution has fundamentally altered investor behavior, with monthly flows now exceeding INR300 billion and 98 percent of accounts committed for over 36 months, meaning that equity market volatility no longer creates earning cyclicality for well-positioned asset managers—rather, flows have become structural and resilient. SBI Funds Management is uniquely positioned to capture this entire opportunity set through its unreplicable distribution architecture: the company commands 23,265 SBI branches, engagement with 100 million YONO digital users, 134,000 nationwide distribution partners, and a proprietary platform reaching 4.1 million users, collectively accounting for approximately 20 percent of overall AUM and 35 percent of equity AUM. With less than 2 percent of SBI's eligible customer base currently penetrated, this represents a multi-year runway for customer acquisition. Operationally, SBIFUNDS has engineered industry-leading cost efficiency at 8 basis points of AUM—a function of leveraging SBI's existing infrastructure rather than building new branches—with continued operating leverage expected to compress this to 7 basis points by FY28, supporting EBITDA margins approaching 81 percent at scale. The revenue growth narrative is multi-faceted: the equity allocation within the fund portfolio has surged from 30 percent in FY21 to 46 percent currently, driving yield expansion from 30 basis points to 35 basis points, while newly launched high-yield products like the SIF business have already captured 25.8 percent market share within quarters; simultaneously, institutional businesses including PMS and AIFs are scaling rapidly and carry structurally higher yields than mass-market products. Management expects 13 percent MF AUM CAGR and 14 percent revenue CAGR through FY28, underpinned by 16 percent PAT CAGR and sustainable 51-52 percent returns on equity. The critical catalyst to monitor is the pace at which SBI's customer base penetration accelerates into systematic investment plans, particularly within Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities where financial asset ownership remains nascent; conversely, the primary risk stems from regulatory changes to TER structures or any compression in active equity fund yields, which could force margin pressure despite strong AUM growth.
